commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
[Hero] Export pinned native checkpoints for inference (#9584)

Export one pinned permanent native Hero checkpoint to BF16 split-expert Hugging Face files. Sampling and export share Grug's checkpoint loader and master-weight detection. Both apply the checkpoint's pending router-bias update from quantile balancing before converting weights. Resume verifies shard identity, size and a freshly computed SHA-256. Completed destinations are refused; the completion manifest is written last.

Keep the layer-at-a-time gathering of the [previously run experimental exporter](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/da624140b92912c2bfef705320a477b91b8df4de/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/ops/export_vllm.py). Every device must fit the largest expert bank; process zero stages one layer plus serialization buffers. Each destination needs one exporting gang and an immutable source. Levanter's HF writer produces matching output with a split-expert adapter, but its current API lacks verified resume and failure propagation to every rank. In a two-rank probe, process zero raised while the other rank remained blocked for eight seconds until the harness terminated it. Snowball's format stays unchanged.

The CPU fixture matches all 76 tensor names, shapes, dtypes and bits and the HF config of the experimental producer. Legacy OCDBT and directory-backed restore checks pass. Two JAX ranks recover from interrupted upload and stop on same-size corruption. Lint and types pass. The broader safe suite has 2,313 passes and the same eight TaskTrove failures independently reproduced on [main at 44a4188c](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/44a4188c197a4b5a314e40cc653f150fa9687dcf).

Earlier H100/GB200 fixture exports and vLLM readback matched all 76 tensors through loading and combining expert projections into 56 parameters. They used [split-loader source 39e62869](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/commit/39e62869) with kernels from the [01911be34fac wheel](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/releases/tag/marin-vllm-gpu-20260924-01911be34fac). Reports are at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/romain/hero-export-producer-01a0efa4/evidence/`. This cleanup has no fresh GPU or full Hero export. Publishing and qualifying x86_64 and aarch64 wheels containing the split loader and layerwise reload remain with [MSRL #799](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/799).

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[rigging] Expose filesystem transfers as a library API (#9606)

Expose copy, transfer planning, synchronization, and streaming hashes
under `rigging.filesystem` so Python callers can use them without
importing `rigging.fsutil`. Add `copy(source_url, destination_url, ...)`
for single-source transfers while retaining the plan/execute APIs for
inspection and multiple sources.

Update callers to the new module paths. Copy semantics and backend
routing remain unchanged; digest formatting stays in the CLI package.

---------

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[RL] Use Megatron for Iceball, Qwen and TaskTrove training (#9507)

Run Iceball, Qwen curriculum RL and TaskTrove through the explicitly
selected Megatron training profile. These callers use the existing
runtime-profile API. Qwen retains its training microbatch and node
allocations. TaskTrove permits four turns and serializes task-selection
enums in its launch document. Iceball uses W&B and captures rollout
logprobs; its AIME smoke evaluation uses Evalchemy with debug mode.

Iceball’s H100 validation completes eight RL steps, restores step-six
policy, optimizer, scheduler, trainer and rollout state, and exports a
verified HF policy consumed by both GSM8K and AIME evaluation records.
GSM8K scores one of 128 questions with flexible extraction; bounded AIME
scores zero of two questions with ten samples each. These runs use the
existing Levanter pretraining/SFT artifact and report zero raw
advantage. A fresh [one-step telemetry
run](https://wandb.ai/atqamar-oa/marin-iceball-micro/runs/i2nzccep) at
runtime `b7814de0` emits both trainer/rollout probability-ratio metrics
and saves a checkpoint.

TaskTrove’s H100x8 smoke completes 16 final verifier results, one update
and checkpoint at 128 GB; a separate run verifies policy-only HF export.
Rewards and gradients are zero, so these runs establish execution and
checkpoint/export integration. Its public smoke-builder test renders a
launch document through YAML and JSON; omitting enum serialization
reproduces the YAML error.

The final broad CPU lane passes at `ae620f1a7d`, with tracked snapshot
fixtures and isolated local artifact prefixes inside an Iris CPU pod.
Changed-file lint and type checks pass. The external launcher lock
selects an immutable revision from MarinSkyRL main.

Part of marin-community/MarinSkyRL#809.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[levanter] Prefetch W&B metric transfers before converting them (#9600)

W&B payload conversion now starts the device-to-host copy for every
`jax.Array` leaf before reading any of them. It previously read each
scalar with its own blocking copy. On the 535B-A23B Hero run that cost
was most of the host time between optimizer steps: about 0.19 s per
update for 780 router values, and 0.77 s on the watch updates every 10
steps, which log 3,572 values
([attribution](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9205#issuecomment-5901019798)).

On one GB200, with Hero-shaped payloads produced by a jitted function,
converting 828 router-metric leaves took 175 ms before and 58 ms after
(median of 120 trials). Converting 3,592 leaves including watch stats
took 740 ms before and 269 ms after. A plain `jax.device_get` of the
same payloads took 53 ms and 255 ms, so about 70 µs per leaf remains.
Packing per-layer metrics into fewer arrays would remove most of that.

Non-primary hosts still materialize payloads while suppressing W&B
output, as #5415 requires. The comment that described suppressed
trackers as no-ops is corrected.

Part of #9205

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[fray] Add AMD Instinct MI300X, MI325X and MI350X device FLOPS (#9568)

Add peak FLOP/s entries for the AMD Instinct MI300X, MI325X and MI350X,
and map JAX device kind strings that contain those model names to them.
`DEVICE_FLOPS` had no AMD entries, so Levanter logged no MFU on AMD
GPUs.

The values are the dense peaks from AMD's datasheets. The
structured-sparsity figures are twice as large and are left out, which
matches how the NVIDIA entries are stored. For fp32 and fp64 the entries
use the matrix figure. The MI325X has the same compute as the MI300X
(304 compute units at 2100 MHz), so its values are identical.

The MI350X datasheet lists 2.3096 PFLOPs for FP16 and BF16 but 4.614 for
FP8 and INT8, which is twice 2.307. The entries use the published
numbers. If 2.3096 is a misprint, bf16 MFU on the MI350X reads about
0.1% low. The MI350X datasheet publishes no TF32 figure, so that entry
has none.

Under ROCm 7.1.0 with JAX 0.11.2, JAX reports `AMD Instinct MI300X` and
`AMD Instinct MI350X` as the device kind, and both map to the new
entries (verified on an AMD HPC Fund cluster; see the PR comments). The
MI325X was not tested and is assumed to follow the same pattern.

Part of #9462
